tickets.title: As a Chef, I want to mark any menu item as 'Sold Out' instantly from my kitchen display te
tickets.description:
1. Pass if tapping the "Sold Out" button updates the local kitchen screen interface state within 1 second.
   2. Pass if the system queues the status update and syncs it to the live cloud menu database immediately upon network restoration.

tickets.title: As a Student with a nut allergy, I want to apply a 'No Peanuts' filter to the mobile menu
tickets.description:
1. Pass if checking the 'No Peanuts' constraint immediately filters out and excludes all peanut-tagged food items from the display grid.
2. Pass if the applied allergen profile filter configuration persists across active user session reloads.

tickets.title: As a Student, I want to place and pay for my lunch order on my mobile phone while walking
tickets.description:
1. Pass if the mobile system successfully processes the transaction and renders a secure order confirmation QR code.
   2. Pass if the generated order is dispatched to the kitchen terminal queue in real-time under stable connectivity.

tickets.title: As a Student, I want my mobile ordering session to handle minor Wi-Fi drops gracefully
tickets.description: 1. Pass if active shopping cart state parameters remain fully intact inside client-side local storage during network transitions.

analysis.ambiguity1: The requirement "to order food on their phone while they are walking from class" is too vague regarding its platform target. It fails to specify whether the system must be delivered as a native mobile application (iOS/Android) or a mobile-responsive web application, affecting testing boundaries.
analysis.ambiguity2: The marketing requirement to "send push notifications to students at 11:30 AM" is ambiguous. It does not define how the system should handle OS-level user permission denials or how it manages delivery constraints if a student's device is completely offline in a basement classroom.
analysis.conflictSolution:
Conflict: The Chef needs the ability to mark items as "Sold Out" instantly to prevent invalid orders, but the IT Infrastructure Team warns that the basement Wi-Fi is terrible and the kitchen display system must operate offline for up to 10 minutes without crashing.

Resolution: Implement a local caching and queued synchronization layer on the Kitchen Display System (KDS). When the Chef marks an item as "Sold Out" during a network drop, the state is immediately applied to the local kitchen screen and queued. Once the Wi-Fi connection automatically re-establishes within the 10-minute threshold, the queued state updates sync to the cloud database, instantly updating the mobile application menu for students.
analysis.nfr1: The kitchen display system must include a local data persistence layer that enables continuous offline operations for at least 10 minutes during Wi-Fi disconnections.
analysis.nfr2: The mobile menu application must execute strict client-side data filtering to completely hide allergen-containing items based on active user profile restrictions.
analysis.nfr3: The order routing system architecture must minimize processing bottlenecks to scale effectively and reduce peak physical queue times below 20 minutes.
